original_question: Can the particle-rotor description of chiral doublet bands be reformulated so that the rigid core is replaced by a collective Hamiltonian whose parameters are extracted microscopically from constrained triaxial mean-field calculations, thereby incorporating vibration-rotation coupling into chirality studies in a genuinely microscopic way?
target_in_paper: “Open problems in the interpretation of the observed pair of near degenerate ΔI = 1 bands with the same parity as the chiral doublet bands are discussed … including the description of quantum tunneling in the mean field approximation as well as the deformation, core polarization and configuration of the particle rotor model (PRM). Future developments of the theoretical approach are prospected.”
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the need to go beyond the rigid-core particle-rotor model by replacing the rotor with a collective Hamiltonian, extracting its parameters from microscopic triaxial mean-field calculations, and thereby incorporating vibration–rotation coupling in a microscopic framework.
missing_details: Specify that the model targets odd–odd triaxial nuclei exhibiting ΔI = 1 chiral doublet bands with identical parity
Define the collective Hamiltonian as two-dimensional in azimuthal (ϕ) and polar (θ) degrees of freedom
State that the collective potential and mass parameters are to be obtained from constrained tilted-axis cranking covariant density functional (or relativistic mean-field) calculations
Mention that the standard PRM couples two high-j quasiparticles (e.g. πh₁₁/₂⊗νh₁₁/₂) to a rigid triaxial rotor with fixed deformation γ
Include the goal of describing quantum tunneling between left- and right-handed configurations via the collective Hamiltonian
Quantify that the replacement aims to capture both chiral vibration and static chiral rotation regimes
refined_question: In odd–odd triaxially deformed nuclei that exhibit near-degenerate ΔI = 1 chiral doublet bands with the same parity, can one construct a two-dimensional collective Hamiltonian on the polar (θ) and azimuthal (ϕ) orientations of the rotational axis—replacing the rigid triaxial core in the particle-rotor model (which couples two high-j quasiparticles, e.g. πh₁₁/₂⊗νh₁₁/₂, to a fixed-deformation rotor)—where the collective potential and mass parameters are extracted microscopically from constrained tilted-axis cranking mean-field (relativistic density functional) calculations? Would such a formulation incorporate vibration–rotation coupling and enable a fully microscopic description of quantum tunneling between left- and right-handed chiral configurations?
justification: The target statement is the abstract’s concluding prospect for future theoretical developments of the PRM (turn7view0 lines 37–40). The draft aligns with this but omits the paper’s specific focus on odd–odd triaxial nuclei with πh₁₁/₂⊗νh₁₁/₂ configuration, the two-dimensional nature of the collective Hamiltonian, and the origin of its parameters in constrained tilted-axis cranking calculations. The refined question makes these explicit, remains faithful to the paper’s narrow scope, and incorporates necessary definitions for self-containment.
